issues.description: Three lock-guard negative Send implementations contain two consecutive commas in their generic parameter lists, leaving an empty generic parameter and preventing the source from parsing.
issues.rationale: The problem snapshot contains impl<T /*?Sized*/,, G: SpinGuardian> for WriteGuard, ReadGuard and UpgradeableGuard. Comments are ignored by the lexer, so the parser sees impl<T,,G...>, an empty generic parameter. This is a single formatting-induced syntax root repeated three times, independent of verifier proof reasoning. The direct next PR commit changes all three lists to impl<T /*: ?Sized*/, G: SpinGuardian>. The enabled sync/rwlock module cannot be parsed with the malformed lists; the fix removes the extra comma without changing guard semantics.
issues.verification: Historical project Verus not executed. Source syntax and exact repair verified. An independent rustc 1.88.0 minimal generic impl containing the same doubled comma failed with expected one of #, >, const, identifier, or lifetime, found comma. This confirms parsing mechanics, not a complete historical project build.
